what_its_for: This medicine combines two ingredients to help you at night. Ibuprofen relieves pain, reduces fever, and eases inflammation. Diphenhydramine helps you fall asleep. Together, they are used to treat minor aches and pains (like headache, backache, muscle aches, or minor arthritis pain) that make it hard to sleep. This is a nighttime pain reliever and sleep aid only — it is NOT meant to be used during the day or as a regular sleep aid.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with a full glass of water (8 ounces). Take it with food or milk if it upsets your stomach. Only take it at bedtime, right before you are ready to go to sleep. Do not crush or chew tablets — swallow them whole. Do not take more than the recommended dose, and do not take it for longer than 2 weeks without talking to your doctor.
dosing: Adults and children 12 years and older: Take 2 tablets (ibuprofen 200 mg / diphenhydramine 25 mg each) at bedtime only. That is a total of 400 mg ibuprofen and 50 mg diphenhydramine per dose. Do NOT take more than 2 tablets in 24 hours. Children under 12 years old should NOT use this medicine unless their doctor specifically tells them to.
missed_dose: This medicine is taken only at bedtime when needed, so a regular dosing schedule does not apply. If you forget to take it and you are still planning to sleep for a full 7 to 8 hours, you may take it then. If you are no longer able to get a full night of sleep, skip the dose entirely. Never double up on doses.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in a dry place away from heat, light, and moisture — do NOT store it in a bathroom medicine cabinet or near the kitchen sink. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT drink alcohol while taking this medicine — it can make the drowsiness much worse and increase the risk of stomach bleeding. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert or fully awake. Avoid taking other sleep aids, antihistamines (like Benadryl or NyQuil), or other medicines containing diphenhydramine at the same time. Avoid other NSAIDs like aspirin, naproxen (Aleve), or other ibuprofen products while using this medicine. Avoid if you have had stomach ulcers, kidney disease, or heart disease unless your doctor says it is safe.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: black, tarry, or bloody stools; vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds; severe stomach pain; swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat (signs of allergic reaction); hives or difficulty breathing; chest pain; sudden weight gain or swelling in your legs or feet; little or no urination; or yellowing of your skin or eyes. Also call your doctor if your pain gets worse or lasts more than 10 days, if you develop a new fever, or if your sleep problems do not improve after 2 weeks.
when_it_works: The diphenhydramine (sleep aid) usually starts working within 30 minutes of taking this medicine, so take it right before bed. The ibuprofen (pain reliever) typically begins to work within 20 to 30 minutes and reaches its strongest effect within 1 to 2 hours. The pain relief can last 4 to 6 hours.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older): Use with extra caution. Diphenhydramine can cause serious confusion, dizziness, falls, and memory problems in older adults. Ibuprofen increases the risk of stomach bleeding and kidney problems with age. Talk to your doctor before using this product if you are 65 or older. Pregnant women: Do NOT use ibuprofen after 20 weeks of pregnancy unless directed by a doctor, as it may harm the unborn baby. Diphenhydramine should also be used with caution during pregnancy. Breastfeeding mothers: Both ingredients can pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before using. People with certain health conditions: Avoid or use with caution if you have kidney disease, liver disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, stomach ulcers, glaucoma, enlarged prostate, or asthma. Always tell your doctor and pharmacist about all medications and supplements you take.
